title: PyTorch CNN Layer Building & Shape Mismatch Debugging
raw_content:
[00:00 - 08:00] Open Google Colab. We import torch and torch.nn as nn. We build SimpleCNN with self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=3, out_channels=16, kernel_size=3, padding=1). Setting padding=1 keeps 32x32 spatial dimensions.
[08:00 - 20:00] We add self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2) and self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1). After two convolutions and pools, tensor shape is (B, 32, 8, 8).
[20:00 - 42:00] Run the forward cell: an error occurred! RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (64x2048 and 1024x10). Why did this happen? After x.view(x.size(0), -1), flattened features are 32*8*8 = 2048. But self.fc1 was written as nn.Linear(1024, 10). To fix this, change in_features to 2048. Never include the batch dimension B in in_features.
[42:00 - 55:00] Configure loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss() and optimizer = optim.Adam(lr=0.001). Inside loop: optimizer.zero_grad() -> forward -> loss -> loss.backward() -> optimizer.step().
[55:00 - 60:00] Training loss drops from 2.14 to 0.42 after 5 epochs. Always verify tensor dimensions at each layer.
supporting_materials_text:
```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

class SimpleCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(SimpleCNN, self).__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 16, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1)
        # Fixed dimension: 32 * 8 * 8 = 2048
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(32 * 8 * 8, 10)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.pool(self.relu(self.conv1(x)))
        x = self.pool(self.relu(self.conv2(x)))
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        return self.fc1(x)
```
